A_general.open_code_note: No official public repository or package was found in the prepared evidence or web search. ICE's published connector documentation describes the hosted service; it does not identify public server code.
other_official_servers: ICE describes ICE Aurora for Desktop, ICE Chat, and ICE Compass as other AI or data channels. Public evidence does not identify these as MCP endpoints.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: ICE publishes no MCP-specific price in the reviewed material. Access requires an active ICE Data Services account with applicable licenses for the content sets and MFA-enabled ICE SSO.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The connector requires applicable ICE Data Services licenses. Public pages reviewed provide no plan names or prices.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: ICE says its MCP connector prices delivered data value rather than LLM compute volume; an example result is quoted before the query and aggregated across users at the firm. Actual tariffs and units are not published in the reviewed sources.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Existing customer entitlements govern data access. ICE documents MFA-enabled SSO, coverage beginning January 2026, and that queries spanning more than one month may time out. No public rate limit or quota was found.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: ICE controls account, license, and entitlement access; the organization controls its ICE account and licensed content. Specific administrative controls are not documented publicly.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The Anthropic directory labels the connector Read; its six names appear retrieval, classification, or computation oriented. The endpoint schemas and tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were unavailable, so those annotations and effects could not be verified. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow is documented; the endpoint could not be inspected. 3. ICE requires an active account, applicable licenses, MFA, and existing customer entitlements. OAuth scopes and role inheritance details are not public in the reviewed evidence. 4. ICE documents search guidance, a seven-calendar-day default when no date range is specified, January 2026 data coverage, and possible timeouts for ranges over one month. No read-only mode, tool filtering, or sandbox endpoint was found. 5. ICE says entitlements govern access and ICE does not store query/session data beyond the connection. Field-level masking and data-boundary details are not documented. 6. Queries spanning over one month may time out; single-day or weekly windows are recommended. No rate limits, per-call costs, or response truncation details found. 7. Issuer-name resolution is documented. Parameter validation, coercion, correction, and operator overrides are unknown. 8. ICE says it does not store query/session data beyond the connection; audit logging and telemetry are not documented. 9. No feedback/rating tool appears in the six-name directory list. ICE invites users to contact support with connector questions, issues, or feedback. No tool-result upsell or marketing elicitation was documented. 10. ICE describes its embedded methodology knowledge layer; no MCP-delivered skills or behavioral tool instructions were published. 11. ICE says Claude maintains context about previous queries; no server-side memory behavior is documented. 12. ICE describes a knowledge layer and orchestration across rate, issuer, and bond data; no nested MCP servers are described. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or general-purpose escape-hatch tool is listed in the available names. Schemas were unavailable.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: "Use single-day or weekly date ranges for the fastest query performance. Queries spanning more than one month may time out."
"If no date range is specified, the system defaults to the last 7 calendar days."
"Reference bonds by issuer name for convenient lookups. The MCP connector resolves issuers to the correct identifiers behind the scenes."
"Specify an asset category (corporate, municipal, agency, securitized) to focus your query and improve performance."
"Use the sector filter (Financial, Industrial, Utility) to narrow corporate bond queries."
"Use aggregation (group by sector, issuer, date, or hour) for volume analysis instead of requesting thousands of individual records."
"Ask follow-up questions — Claude maintains context about your previous queries."
"Use the knowledge layer for definitions: ask \"What is an institutional trade?\" rather than assuming thresholds."
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The public directory presents one endpoint and one flat list of six tools. ICE documents internal methodology and data orchestration, but no nested MCP servers or dynamically loaded toolsets. The endpoint itself could not be inspected.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: ICE's official connector page does not publish a tool list or total. Anthropic's Claude connector directory lists six names, and the connector URL matches the input endpoint. Agentman reports six names copied from Anthropic's directory; PromptArmor reports the same six with null descriptions and the directory UUID, so it is not independent enumeration. mcpservers.org describes capabilities but does not list tool names. No catalogue-only tools were added. The available names and details are in actions.json.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: ICE recommends single-day or weekly ranges for speed, narrowing by asset category or sector, aggregating volume analysis, and using issuer names for lookups. It says queries over one month may time out. The public documentation does not establish whether these recommendations are technically enforced or merely guidance.
F_documentation.governance_promises: ICE states: "Access to ICE data is governed by customers' existing ICE entitlements." It also states: "ICE does not store query or session data beyond the duration of your connection with the connector." It directs users to their AI provider's privacy and retention policies for that platform's handling. No MCP-specific retention, redistribution, or AI-training terms were found in the reviewed public pages.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: ICE describes the knowledge layer as applying its fixed-income methodology and mapping securities to an evaluation frame, with structured access to rate, issuer, and bond data. ICE calls the data source consistent and traceable and presents the connector as supporting sourced, methodology-grounded responses.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The entitlement and transient query/session storage statements are official ICE documentation, but no server code or runtime behavior was available to verify enforcement. Query defaults and time-range caveats are documented, while their implementation details remain unverified. Methodology application and cross-layer routing are described by ICE; tool schemas and result provenance could not be inspected. ICE disclaims responsibility for third-party LLM outputs.

contradictions: ICE's connector page describes four data groups and omits FINRA TRACE/MSRB RTRS from its displayed list, while the July 2026 ICE report says Phase 2 added Treasury and AAA municipal curves, end-of-day evaluations, enhanced transparency, and price-verification context beyond TRACE and MSRB content. Anthropic's directory continues to describe TRACE/RTRS trades and bond reference data. This appears consistent with a staged expansion, but the page and listing present different content scopes.

The endpoint and all prepared OAuth metadata probes returned HTTP 403 with “Access Denied,” while Anthropic's directory lists the endpoint and six tools. This prevents direct verification of advertised tool schemas, OAuth metadata, and capabilities.
observations_for_research: ICE describes a server-side methodology layer and security-to-evaluation-frame routing that shape the context available to the model before it reasons over the data.
The documented default time window (last seven calendar days) and the January 2026 coverage start constrain the temporal scope of default and historical queries.

ICE's reported value-based pricing example uses a pre-query quote and aggregates the delivered value across firm users, linking data access to a firm-level commercial model rather than solely to model-compute usage.
